feedback.problem: Calculate the points where the ellipse $\frac{(x+3)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-7)^{2}}{9}=1$ intercepts the $y$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
To calculate the $y$-intercept, we need to substitute $x=0$ in the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $y.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+3)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-7)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(0+3)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-7)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{9}{16}+\frac{(y-7)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ 81+16(y-7)^{2} & =9\cdot 16 \\ 81+16(y-7)^{2} & =144 \\ 16(y-7)^{2} & =63 \\ (y-7)^{2} & =\frac{63}{16} \\ y-7 & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{63}{16}} \\ y-7 & =\pm \frac{3\sqrt{7}}{4} \\ y & =7\pm \frac{3\sqrt{7}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $y$-axis at the points $(0,7-\frac{3\sqrt{7}}{4})$ and $(0,7+\frac{3\sqrt{7}}{4}).$
